Key Observations

Technical differentiation

Companies split into roughly three technical tiers:

  1. Genome-wide or large-panel cfDNA methylation sequencing — GRAIL, Burning Rock, Singlera. These interrogate tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of CpG sites and rely heavily on ML classifiers for both cancer detection and tissue-of-origin prediction. Highest information content but also highest cost and analytical complexity.

  2. Targeted qPCR methylation of specific validated loci — Nucleix, Epigenomics, MDxHealth, Genomictree. These anchor on a small number of well-validated methylation markers (e.g., SEPT9, SHOX2, OTX1) and use PCR-based quantification. More commercially mature, lower cost, and further along in regulatory clearance — but inherently single-cancer or narrow-scope.

  3. Hybrid multi-analyte approaches — Exact Sciences (CancerGuard), Guardant (Shield). These combine methylation signals with somatic mutation profiles and/or protein biomarkers to boost sensitivity, particularly for early-stage cancers where cfDNA shedding is low.

BillionToOne sits in a distinct niche: their QCT™ technology turns methylation into a precise quantitative tumor burden metric (absolute molecule counting) rather than a binary detection signal, making it better suited for longitudinal treatment monitoring than early detection screening.

Commercial maturity spectrum

Nucleix (Bladder EpiCheck) and Epigenomics AG (Epi proColon) are the oldest players with actual regulatory clearances. However, Epigenomics AG is now in financial restructuring (asset sale to New Day Diagnostics pending as of 2024). The urine-based bladder cancer niche (Nucleix, MDxHealth, Genomictree) is more commercially mature than the blood-based MCED space, because the signal-to-noise problem is more tractable in urine for a single organ.

Among blood-based MCED players, GRAIL’s Galleri is the furthest along commercially (LDT, NHS pilot, Pathfinder 2 study n=35,000). Guardant’s Shield MCD and BillionToOne’s Northstar Response are commercially launched as LDTs. Most others remain in clinical validation or development.

Geographic split

Several methylation-based MCED tests have advanced further in Asia before entering US/EU markets:

  • Burning Rock (OverC / ELSA-seq): CE mark obtained 2022; extensive China-based validation studies (THUNDER, PREDICT, PRESCIENT); FDA Breakthrough Designation obtained subsequently.
  • Singlera Genomics (PanSeer): large retrospective validation conducted in collaboration with Fudan University; detection up to 4 years pre-clinical diagnosis demonstrated.
  • Genomictree (EarlyTect): approved in Korea; validation studies primarily in East Asian cohorts.

This geographic pattern reflects both the high GI cancer burden in East Asia (making CRC, liver, and esophageal cancers natural targets) and more accessible early-stage regulatory and study infrastructure in China and Korea.

The Adela distinction

Adela (formerly known as Grail’s spinout focus for non-blood approaches) uses a cfDNA methylation approach that also incorporates fragmentation patterns — recognizing that nucleosome positioning leaves interpretable marks on cfDNA fragment lengths in addition to the methylation signal itself. This multi-modal epigenetic signal may improve sensitivity at low tumor fractions.
